approach: One shared acceptance function `check_stored_reading` (reading.rs) calls the existing `check_reading_acceptance(reading, &request.text, None, &[])`. The new `athena check-reading --request <file> --reading <file>` prints `accept` or `refuse: <reason>` from it. Before the verifier, `produce_and_verify` runs a replay step. It takes the newest 50 requests whose job has an accepted reading (`Job.accepted_reading`, from `Records::load` at the base commit). It asks a base checker and a candidate checker about each, and lists the requests the base accepts and the candidate refuses. The checkers are built from the two trees (checkout, build, run `check-reading`). In the resolver, a `#[cfg(test)]` override is consulted first, in front of tree resolution and the subcommand probe. The result is a new typed record `athena.replay/1` at `<job>/replay.json` (`Replay`, patterned on `Baseline`). Held means newly_refused*100 > total*REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT (code constant 10), unless the accepted reading's criteria state an intent to refuse more. A held replay becomes an Athena-sourced Blocker finding plus a reason through `verify::apply_replay_hold(&mut Judgment, &Replay)`. It is called immediately after `judge()`, before the `Verification` literal, so the stored verdict, findings and state agree (Rejected, not landed). `store.rs::job_of` names the new kind so `Records::load` does not panic. The verifier brief carries a size-capped replay summary, or `no replay: <reason>`. Nothing in the replay calls a model. The replay's build directory is removed, and the build wall time recorded, before the pre-verifier disk gate runs.

decisions.choice: New record kind `athena.replay/1` at `<job>/replay.json`: `AnyRecord::Replay(Box<Replay>)` in records.rs (schema const, `validate`, `canonical_path`, `schema()`), and `store.rs::job_of` returns `Some(&r.job)` for it. `JobRecords` gets no new field: `JobRecords::add` already ignores unnamed kinds in its `other =>` arm. A test shows `Records::load` on a tree with a replay.json does not panic.
decisions.reason: Finding 1 is right. `Records::load` falls to `other => job_of(&other).expect(..)`, and `job_of` ends in `_ => None` (store.rs:324-331, 253-270), so an unnamed kind would panic every later load: status, land, and the next job's replay. Adding one `job_of` arm fixes it with a one-line change to a non-governance file, now a deliverable. The gate's job loaders use `_ => {}` arms for kinds they do not name, so the records check accepts the file.

rejected.why: `Verification` is a struct literal in about 10 places in non-deliverable files.
`JobRecords { .. }` literals in steward.rs, status.rs and reading.rs tests would need edits. Nothing reads the slot.
Out of scope; it is what failed job 20261028-034820-v3rf.

decisions.choice: `verify::apply_replay_hold(&mut Judgment, &Replay)` is called in run/mod.rs right after `judge(..)` returns, with `let mut judgment`, before the `Verification` literal (run/mod.rs:2368-2382). It adds an Athena-sourced Blocker finding naming the list and a reason, and sets `final_verdict` to Fail. The existing lines that set `verification_passed`, `state` and `verified(&judgment, ..)` then follow from the changed judgment.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: the `Verification` literal copies `judgment.findings`, `final_verdict` and `reasons`, so a later change would store Pass next to Rejected. `VerdictInputs` stays unchanged, so its test literals are untouched.

decisions.choice: The threshold is `REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT: usize = 10` in reading.rs, with the integer test `newly_refused * 100 > total * REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT`. The window is `REPLAY_WINDOW: usize = 50`.
decisions.reason: A code constant is required. Integer maths makes exactly 10% not held (5 of 50) and 6 of 50 held, with no float rounding.

decisions.choice: The replay always runs, with no flag, diff matching or skip switch. Cheap checks come first: empty history, then a tree without `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml`, then build and probe. Any failure records `no replay: <reason>` and never fails the job. A nested run records `no replay: nested run`.
decisions.reason: Detecting refusal-rule changes is out of scope. Fixture repositories and non-Athena repositories get a recorded reason with no build.

rejected.option: Run only when the candidate changes reading.rs
rejected.why: That is detecting rule changes by matching diffs, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: The seam is a trait `ReadingChecker { fn check(&self, &Request, &Reading) -> Result<(), String> }` in reading.rs. The production implementation runs `<binary> check-reading` and parses the first output line. The test override is a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local pair of boxed checkers, consulted first in `resolve_replay_checkers`, with a drop guard and a use counter. `check_stored_reading`, the selection, the comparison, the threshold, the record, the finding and the brief are all production code in the tests. The double supplies only the answer a built binary would give.
decisions.reason: This adds no field to `Athena`, which has about 15 constructors outside the deliverables. A built binary is not needed in the pipeline tests.

rejected.why: It breaks every `Athena { .. }` literal outside the deliverables.

rejected.option: An environment variable that fakes or skips the replay
rejected.why: It is a skip switch (out of scope) and leaks into production.

decisions.choice: The base is probed, not assumed. A side whose build lacks `check-reading` makes the replay `no replay: the <base|candidate> build has no check-reading subcommand`. It is neither held nor a pass. The same applies to a build failure, a timeout or unparseable output. A partial count is never recorded.
decisions.reason: The job that lands this change has a base without the subcommand. Treating that as zero refusals would be an empty success. A timeout read as a refusal would hold a good candidate.

rejected.option: Treat a missing base subcommand as zero newly refused
rejected.why: It reports a pass with nothing checked.

decisions.choice: Intent to refuse more is decided by `criteria_intend_higher_refusals(&[Criterion]) -> bool`. It matches a constant list of whole phrases ('refuse more', 'refuses more', 'higher refusal rate', 'more refusals', 'raise the refusal rate') through the existing `has_phrase`. A hit sets held=false; the replay is still recorded with its list and counts.
decisions.reason: The check is deterministic and testable, and the replay stays visible to the verifier.

rejected.option: Ask a model whether the criteria intend more refusals
rejected.why: The replay must make no model call.

decisions.choice: Disk and time. The replay builds both trees in one target directory under the job directory. `replay_reading_rules` removes that directory before it returns, so it is gone before `verifier_environment_problem` (run/mod.rs:2178). `Replay` records `elapsed_s` (build and replay wall time). The progress line shows it.
decisions.reason: Finding 6. The retried job failed at 9.8 of 10 GB free at that gate; the replay must not add to the peak the gate sees.

rejected.option: Leave the target directory for the job's general cleanup
rejected.why: The disk gate would run with the builds still on disk.

The whole section is capped at `REPLAY_SECTION_MAX_BYTES` (4096). With no usable replay it shows `no replay: <reason>`. With `replay = None` the brief is unchanged.
decisions.reason: The brief stays bounded with a very long list, and the full list stays in the record. `VerifierInputs {` literals exist only in run/mod.rs:2112 and the briefs.rs tests, all deliverables (finding 4).

rejected.why: 50 long reasons can exceed any size limit.

risks.risk: Building both trees on every Athena-workspace job is slow and fills disk. The retried job failed at the pre-verifier disk gate.
risks.mitigation: Cheap checks (empty history, no athena-cli package) come before any build. Both builds share one target directory under the job directory, and `replay_reading_rules` removes it before returning, so it is gone before `verifier_environment_problem` runs. The builds use the check timeout. `elapsed_s` in the record shows the cost. A build or probe failure records `no replay: <reason>` and never fails the job.

risks.risk: A flaky or timed-out subprocess is read as a refusal and holds a good candidate.
risks.mitigation: Only a successful run that prints `refuse: ...` counts as a refusal. Any other exit, a timeout or unparseable output makes the whole replay a recorded `no replay: <reason>`, never a partial count.

risks.risk: The first landing's base lacks `check-reading`, so the replay cannot run for it.
risks.mitigation: The probe records 'no replay: the base build has no check-reading subcommand'. The verifier sees it, and the CHANGELOG says so. It is neither a pass nor a hold.

risks.risk: The thread-local override leaks between tests, or the pipeline runs on another thread.
risks.mitigation: A drop guard clears it. Tests assert an override-consulted counter. The override is `#[cfg(test)]`, so production has no switch.

risks.risk: A new `AnyRecord` variant breaks an exhaustive match elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: The compiler finds each. Grep shows the matches that name record kinds are in records.rs and store.rs, both handled; the gate loaders use `_ =>` arms. Report any other site in the output instead of editing an undeclared file.
Boundary tests at 5 of 50 (not held), 6 of 50 (held), and 3 of 10 (held).

risks.risk: The size cap truncates a held list so the verifier cannot see every id.
risks.mitigation: The brief points to replay.json, and the Blocker finding's evidence carries the ids. Ids are short and the cap is 4096 bytes.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in main.rs. It writes a fixture request and two fixture readings to a temp directory as `AnyRecord` JSON: a clean reading and one whose criterion evidence is only 'the producer's report lists X'. It calls the production handler with `--request` and `--reading` paths (the clap parse of `check-reading` plus the function that prints). It asserts `accept` for the clean one and a line starting `refuse:` with the rule's reason text for the other. It then asserts both lines equal what `athena_core::reading::check_reading_acceptance` gives directly on the same values. The handler returns its line as a String so the test needs no process spawn. The subcommand is added in step 9. The core function exists today.
demonstrations.observes: Both outputs appear. The refuse line carries the reason. The output equals the reading.rs result.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no subcommand the parse fails. With no call to `check_reading_acceptance`, the two fixtures print the same line.

demonstrations.method: Test in reading.rs calling the production `replay_readings(records, &base, &candidate, criteria)` over 12 in-memory jobs (request, reading, job with `accepted_reading`). The base is the real `check_stored_reading` behind `ReadingChecker`. The candidate wraps the same real function and also refuses readings whose title starts 'T-', a candidate-like rule change. One 'T-' job is also refused by the base. The checkers are passed as `&dyn ReadingChecker` arguments, a seam step 3 adds. The test asserts the newly refused ids are exactly the 'T-' jobs the base accepts, that the count matches, and that the base-refused 'T-' job is not listed.
demonstrations.observes: The exact list and count of requests refused by the candidate and accepted by the base.
demonstrations.fails_without: A replay that lists all candidate refusals, or ignores the base, includes the base-refused request or gets the count wrong.

demonstrations.method: Tests in reading.rs calling the production `replay_inputs(&Records, REPLAY_WINDOW)` and `replay_readings`. (a) 60 jobs with accepted readings plus 5 jobs with `accepted_reading` None: the selected ids are exactly the newest 50 by `received_at`, none of the unaccepted. (b) An empty `Records` gives status NoReplay, a reason starting 'no replay: ', total 0 and held false; its text rendering is never a pass. The `Records` fixtures are built in memory (`Records::default()` and `JobRecords`, which exist today); `replay_inputs` is added in step 3.
demonstrations.observes: Window size, newest-first order, exclusion of unaccepted readings, and the empty-history result.
demonstrations.fails_without: An oldest-first or unfiltered selection gives different ids. An empty history treated as zero refusals gives no 'no replay' reason.

demonstrations.method: Tests in reading.rs calling the production `replay_readings` and the hold rule over fixtures of 50 readings: 6 newly refused (held, list present), 5 newly refused (exactly 10%, not held), 0 newly refused, and 6 newly refused where the candidate criteria contain 'the checker refuses more readings' (not held, but the returned `Replay` still carries the list and counts). A small-total case (3 of 10, held) is included. The candidate checker is an injected `&dyn ReadingChecker` that refuses chosen ids.

demonstrations.fails_without: A `>=` comparison holds the 5-of-50 case. With no intent rule the fourth case is held.

Preconditions: a committed repository fixture whose records hold 12 jobs with accepted readings, written through the real record writers; the fake producer changes a file. The `#[cfg(test)]` override is set with a candidate checker refusing 3 of the 12 (25%), so no cargo build or `--help` probe runs. The test asserts the override counter shows it was consulted. demonstrations.fails_without: If the replay or the hold is not wired, the job lands and there is no finding or replay.json. A free-form replay.md fails the absence assertion. A missing `job_of` arm fails the `Records::load` assertion.

demonstrations.method: Pipeline test in run/mod.rs that runs `athena.go` twice on identical fixtures. Model calls are counted with an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` that the `FakeAgentDriver::new` script closure increments (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:43,60; the script closure exists today), not `requests()` in athena-core fake.rs, which counts pinner calls. Run A uses an override whose candidate checker equals the base (no rule change). Run B uses a candidate refusing 1 of 12 readings (about 8%, under 10%), so both runs follow the same post-verify path and are not held. The test asserts the two counts are equal. It also asserts Run B's replay is non-empty with 1 newly refused, so the replay did run.
demonstrations.observes: Equal model call counts with and without a candidate rule change, and a non-empty replay in the second run.
demonstrations.fails_without: A replay that called a model, for example to judge refusals, would raise the count in Run B only.

open_questions: Whether `athena.go` in the fake pipeline runs `produce_and_verify` on the test's own thread was not confirmed. The thread-local override relies on it. The tests assert an override-consulted counter, so a thread mismatch fails loudly. If a worker thread runs it, switch the override to a process-wide `Mutex<Option<..>>` guarded by a test lock.

`Snapshot::create(.., SnapshotRepo::Base)` was seen only at its call site. Whether it gives a plain checkout of a named commit usable for a build must be confirmed by the producer. Otherwise the resolver checks out with `git worktree`-free `git archive` through the existing `Git` wrapper.
The 'intends a higher rate' phrase list is a judgment. Maintainers may want other phrases.

The replay checks the stored request and reading only, with no earlier attempt or referenced jobs. Rules that need earlier jobs (`check_prior_result_and_scope` for retries) pass trivially in the replay. Whether that is enough was not settled.
Which existing tests, if any, check docs/records.md against the record kinds was not searched. If one exists, the new row must match its format.
